newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says Belarus referndum result "normal".
newsitem.headline: Russia says Belarus referndum result "normal".

text.p: Russia greeted Belarus's controversial referendum on increasing President Alexander Lukashenko's powers as a "normal result" on Monday and said Moscow's bid to defuse the crisis in Minsk had succeeded.

Asked for his assessment of Sunday's vote, which gave Lukashenko massive backing, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said: "The main thing is that Belarus has given its assessment. I think it's a normal result. It's a matter for Belarus."

Earlier, he discussed the referendum results with President Boris Yeltsin. The Kremlin press service said the two men stressed that Russia's "timely" efforts to mediate last week between Lukashenko and his parliamentary opponents had "prevented a social explosion".
Lukashenko's press secretary Valery Tolkachev said Chernomyrdin and Lukashenko had also discussed the result in a telephone call.

"Chernomyrdin congratulated Lukashenko on his success in the referendum and said it was a free choice of the people. He expressed his hope that the democratic process in Belarus would continue to develop," Tolkachev told Reuters.
Chernomyrdin brokered the compromise after all-night talks on Friday. But it fell apart within a day.
He said on Sunday that a group of Belarus legislators were responsible for wrecking the accord, but also expressed irritation with Lukashenko for failing to do enough to make the accord work.

Moscow favours Lukashenko's quest for closer ties with Russia but fears his autocratic style and lack of free-market economic reforms could prove a burden in the two-state union agreed by Yeltsin and the Belarus president last April.

The Kremlin said Chernomyrdin met Yeltsin for an hour and a half at the Barvikha sanatorium near Moscow, where the president is convalescing. It is the longest reported working meeting Yeltsin has had since his heart bypass operation on November 5.
